title: Two Fed Officials Wanted a Hike. Does Your Loan Float?

scenes.vo: Two Fed officials just voted to raise rates. If your loan floats, listen up.

captions.text: Two Fed officials just voted to raise rates.
If your loan floats, listen up.

scenes.vo: The Fed sets one rate, for overnight bank loans. Other rates stack on top.
Its range tops out at 4 percent. Prime sits at 7. Variable loans add a margin.
Illustrative: on a 50,000 dollar home equity line, each quarter-point hike costs about 125 dollars a year.

captions.text: Illustrative: on a $50,000 home equity line,

scenes.vo: Check your loan papers: fixed, or tied to prime?

fedRangeLow.unit: % lower bound, federal funds target range
fedRangeLow.period: set Oct 28, 2026 (held); no FOMC meeting since

fedRangeHigh.unit: % upper bound, federal funds target range

vote.unit: FOMC vote; Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack preferred a 1/4-point increase

prime.unit: % Bank Prime Loan Rate (rate posted by a majority of top 25 insured U.S.-chartered commercial banks)
prime.source: Federal Reserve H.15 via FRED DPRIME, updated Nov 24, 2026 (fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DPRIME)

primeGap.unit: percentage points, prime minus top of Fed range (observed gap, computed in scenes/math.ts; not a legal rule)

helocRule.unit: HELOC variable rate = index (e.g., U.S. prime rate) + lender margin; payments may change even without new draws
helocRule.source: CFPB, 'What you should know about home equity lines of credit', last updated Aug 2022

illustrativeHike.unit: $ per year, Illustrative: $50,000 constant balance x 0.25 percentage point, interest only (about $10.42/month); computed in scenes/math.ts

nextMeeting.source: Federal Reserve FOMC meeting calendar, retrieved 2026-11-19

notes: The Fed held rates on Oct 28, 2026; two of twelve voters dissented in favor of a hike. VO 'voted to raise rates' is the owner-approved wording (dissent preferring a hike); the on-screen headline says 'wanted a hike'.
Prime = top of Fed range + 3 is today's observed gap, not a law; lenders' indexes and margins vary, and some loans have caps or intro rates.
